subject: Discovery recap: Private/VPC deployment requirements for FinHealth - next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@finhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Private/VPC deployment requirements for FinHealth - next steps

Hi Sarah — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have a shared record. Happy to adjust if I missed anything.

Key pain points you shared:
- Regulated workloads (PCI / HIPAA adjacent) requiring strict data residency and auditability.
- No public egress from model hosts allowed except to approved endpoints.
- Requirement for customer-managed keys (AWS KMS and HSM) for both model artifacts and logging/encryption at rest.
- Preference for a Private/VPC deployment (customer VPC, private control plane) or an on-prem air-gapped option for certain environments.
- Performance: inference latency target ~150-250ms p95 for core flows, and predictable throughput for peak batch jobs.

Current stack / environment you mentioned:
- AWS (us-east-1), VPC with strict outbound rules, AWS KMS for most services.
- Existing inference stack is on-prem/VMs for some regulated customers; evaluating cloud-private options.
- Security contact: Alan Barker (security lead) will be involved for the questionnaire and network review.

Success criteria you outlined:
1) Private control plane option that keeps control-plane traffic within FinHealth network (VPC endpoints / PrivateLink).
2) Integration with customer-managed KMS/HSM for zero-knowledge key management.
3) Minimal or auditable egress; allowlist-only outbound to vendor endpoints.
4) Clear deployment/runbook for on-prem air-gapped install if needed.
5) A POC within ~6 weeks and an initial cost/throughput estimate to present to procurement.

Open questions / items we promised to follow up on:
- Marissa (SE) to share a high-level private deployment architecture and a short deployment playbook.
- Security questionnaire (finhealth-security-qa.xlsx) — I attached our SOC2 summary and the QA template for collection.
- Please confirm the network diagram and any firewall/egress exceptions (network_topology.png).
- Confirm whether KMS integration must use AWS KMS exclusively or if HSM (BYO) is required for all keys.

Proposed next steps:
1) SE deep-dive: 30–45 minute session with Marissa + your networking/security folks (Alan) — proposed windows below.
2) We’ll fill in the QA spreadsheet and return it; Marissa will include a short draft architecture for Private and on-prem air-gapped options.
3) Provide a rough order-of-magnitude cost/throughput estimate for a 3-node POC (dedicated private) and for on-prem air-gapped install.

Attachment(s): SOC2_summary.pdf, finhealth-security-qa.xlsx, deployment_playbook_v1.pdf (draft).

Proposed times for SE call (all PT): Wed Mar 4 10:00–11:00, Thu Mar 5 09:00–10:00, Thu Mar 5 14:00–15:00. If none work, tell me a couple of windows that do.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

—
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
redwood.inference.com

From: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@finhealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Alan Barker <alan.barker@finhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Private/VPC deployment requirements for FinHealth - next steps

Thanks for the clear recap, Aditya — this looks right. A few clarifications from our side:

- Timeline: target POC kickoff in 6 weeks (aiming end of April). Procurement needs a rough cost to evaluate in the next 2 weeks.
- KMS: we need AWS KMS integration for keys used in the cloud deployment. For some regulated customers we will require hardware-backed keys (HSM) — that can be BYOK (bring-your-own-key).
- Egress: our VPC policy is "deny by default"; we can open egress to specific IPs/hostnames once we have a list of required endpoints.
- Air-gap: one of our clinics will require an air-gapped installer for on-prem. That is lower priority for the POC but must be a supported path.

Alan (cc'd) is our security lead — he'll own the QA and networking review. Alan, can you confirm whether the attached network diagram is the most recent? We've added a key management subnet since last quarter.

We can do the SE deep-dive on Wed Mar 4 10:00 PT. I’ll invite Alan and our cloud networking lead.

Attachment: network_topology.png (internal diagram).

Thanks,
Sarah
Senior Product Manager, FinHealth
sarah.jones@finhealth.com | +1 (650) 555-0987

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@finhealth.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Private/VPC deployment requirements for FinHealth - next steps

Thanks Sarah — I’ll come prepared for the Wed 10:00 PT session with a short deck and a proposed architecture. Quick technical notes so the call can dive straight into specifics: 

High-level Private deployment options we’ll cover:
- Private control plane in customer VPC using PrivateLink / VPC endpoints. Control traffic stays within FinHealth network; management plane has optional outbound to specific Redwood endpoints via allow-listed NAT or proxy.
- Dedicated model hosts run in customer VPC under their account (IAM role), with optional autoscaling pools for throughput.
- KMS/Key management: Support for AWS KMS CMKs (grant-based access) and HSM/BYOK flows. We can integrate with AWS CloudHSM or an HSM via a key broker depending on your requirements.
- On-prem air-gapped installer: we provide an offline package and documented runbook; initial POC will focus on cloud-private, but we’ll include high-level steps for air-gapped install.
- Network: requirements will be limited — control-plane heartbeat, model artifact sync (pull-only), and optional telemetry to Redwood endpoints. We’ll provide a minimal allow-list for the POC.

Questions for Alan / Networking team (please have answers ready or we can collect on the call):
1) Can you share the NAT/proxy model for egress (eg. do you require an HTTP proxy for all outbound traffic?)
2) Are there corporate approved CA certs for TLS termination inside the VPC?
3) Which subnets should we plan for model hosts (private subnets with route tables)?
4) Any SIEM/Syslog endpoints for audit/log shipping?

Action items we’ll take after Wed call:
- Draft private-VPC architecture (diagram + minimal firewall allow-list).
- Populate the finhealth-security-qa.xlsx with our answers and any follow-up asks.
- Provide a rough OOM cost/throughput for a 3-node POC and for a single on-prem air-gapped node.

I’ve attached a short draft playbook (deployment_playbook_v1.pdf) and will update it after the call. See you Wed 10:00 PT.

—
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Looking forward to the architecture draft and the allow-list.

Best,
Sarah
